title: Indexes and length
learningObjectives: Explain indexes and length and process JavaScript collections correctly.

understand.concept: Array indexes start at zero. The length property is one greater than the highest existing array index in a dense array, and can also change when the array is modified or assigned a larger index. Accessing an absent index returns undefined.
understand.whyItMatters: Index mistakes can skip or duplicate items. Use length in loops and check whether an index exists before relying on its value.
understand.analogy: The index is the slot number; length is the count of positions from the start to the end of the array.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript array and object methods have defined mutation, iteration, and reference semantics.

explain.narrative: The first score is 70, the last score is 91, and the length is 3.

examples.explanation: The first score is 70, the last score is 91, and the length is 3.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the array or object values described.

practise.guidedTask: Write code that reads the first and last array values safely, including the empty-array case.
practise.independentTask: Build a small collection-processing example using arrays and objects. Test empty collections, missing values, and mutation behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates or returns a new value.
Use clear object property names and deliberate copying.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Indexes and length</title></head><body>
<script>const scores=[70,82,91];console.log(scores[0],scores[scores.length-1],scores.length);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: How do you access the last element of a non-empty array using length?
questions.explanation: The last valid index is one less than the array length.

questions.prompt: What should you check when using an array method?
options: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
Whether the array contains strings only
questions.answer: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
questions.explanation: Mutation behaviour matters when arrays are shared across application code.
